items.question: Are these names and contact details connected to real individuals?
items.answer: No. All generated identities are completely fictional combinations from bundled linguistic name datasets. Any resemblance to real living or deceased persons is purely coincidental.

items.question: Why are emails and phone numbers guaranteed safe for development?
items.answer: Emails are exclusively created using RFC 2606 reserved domains (example.com, example.org, example.net) which can never receive spam. US phone numbers use the fictional 555-0100 to 555-0199 test range.

items.question: Does this tool generate Social Security numbers, credit cards, or passports?
items.answer: Strictly no. To prevent misuse, this utility never generates government identification numbers, financial credentials, or private citizen records.

items.question: How can I export generated names for database seeding?
items.answer: You can instantly copy data to your clipboard or download clean CSV and structured JSON files compatible with mock APIs and database seeding scripts.

items.question: Can I generate the same set of test users across multiple runs?
items.answer: Yes. By entering an optional numeric Seed value, the deterministic pseudorandom number generator produces the exact same sequence of names across test sessions.

items.question: How are culturally accurate names selected for each country?
items.answer: The engine bundles curated dictionaries of over 200 first names and 200 family surnames for each supported country: US, UK, India, Pakistan, Canada, and Australia.

items.question: Can I filter identities by gender?
items.answer: Yes. You can select Male, Female, or Random to match the demographic requirements of your mock application or persona testing.

items.question: What age brackets are used for simulated birth dates?
items.answer: Dates of birth are generated within realistic adult ranges (ages 18 to 75) formatted as ISO 8601 YYYY-MM-DD strings.
